newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper strikers, management start meeting.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper strikers, management start meeting.

text.p: The chairman of Somincor, the company that manages Portugal's Neves Corvo copper mine, met representatives of striking miners on Thursday morning, company officials told Reuters.
The officials said the meeting between Alcides Pereira and union leaders began around 0930 GMT. They did not know how long it was expected to last.

Raul Araujo, personnel director at Neves Corvo, had earlier told Reuters he was doubtful any progress could be made in resolving a dispute that has halted production at the 107,000-tonne per year mine since Monday.

The strike was triggered by the company's introduction of Sunday working as part of a bid to boost efficiency at the mine, some 250 km southeast of Lisbon, where copper yields have been falling steadily in recent years.

Union leaders have threatened to step up their action by staging a demonstration outside Somincor's Lisbon headquarters later on Thursday if management does not agree to an immediate return to the six-day shift as a precondition for negotiations on future working practices.
"It looks like they will be going to Lisbon," Araujo said.

The company has accused miners of illegal picketing and of preventing employees who want to work from doing so. But union leaders say that they have only been blocking side entrances and that anybody who wants to enter through the main gate is free to do so.
